name: Interior design and fit-out project
one_line: A commissioned or self-directed physical-space project whose evidence runs from brief and measured survey through concept design, drawings, schedules and specifications, procurement, site installation, and handover; rooms, property, style, materials and trades are values or observations, not new fields.

deterministic: a space-design document set containing a brief or room schedule, a measured survey, plans/elevations/sections or a model, and a materials/finishes or fixture schedule for the same named property or commission

a specification structure with room or location references, item descriptions, manufacturer/product references, finishes, quantities and installation notes; a product catalogue or moodboard alone is not this structure

a procurement structure linking specified items to quotations, purchase orders, lead times, substitutions, delivery status or supplier correspondence, with the design set or property/work reference present

an installation/handover structure containing site instructions, delivery records, installation photographs, snagging items, as-built information, care/maintenance manuals or a practical-completion/handover pack tied to the designed space
a CAD/BIM or presentation file whose sheets, rooms, dimensions, furniture/fixture tags and material references cohere with schedules or issue records; the extension alone never activates the template

a mixed archive whose manifest or labelled cover packet shows one physical-space commission across design, specification, procurement and installation members; archive membership does not copy facts to its members
needs_llm: whether a moodboard, sample board or supplier catalogue is an active design deliverable, a reference download, or a portfolio presentation
whether a contractor quotation and product invoice belong to the same interior project or are unrelated household purchases, property administration, or business procurement
whether a room photograph records site progress, a completed handover, a photoshoot, or an isolated image; visual appearance cannot supply project facts
whether the named organisation is the client, designer, contractor, supplier, property owner, or merely a brand shown in the scheme
whether an address identifies the designed property, a supplier/contractor address, a mailing address, or a photographed location

whether an incomplete specification or drawing set is still an interior project record when the installation phase is absent; design evidence can activate the template without inventing procurement or completion
never_alone: a room name, address, property name, style word, colour, material, furniture brand or product code alone
a CAD/BIM/design_creative source type or .dwg, .rvt, .skp, .3dm, .indd, .pdf, .jpg or .xlsx extension alone
a moodboard, rendered room image, sample photograph or furniture catalogue without a project/commission or space-design neighbourhood
a contractor, architect, designer, supplier, showroom or property-owner name without a role-bearing project context
a purchase order, receipt, invoice, delivery note or calendar appointment alone; these may be procurement or installation members only when the project relation is evidenced
a filename token such as FINAL, APPROVED, CONSTRUCTION, INSTALL or HANDOVER alone; these are possible stage observations, not validated facts
a site photograph or screenshot alone, and never the absence of EXIF as proof of a screenshot or installation record
a generic home-renovation article, plan template, product image or downloaded specification whose purpose is reading/reference rather than making the space

work_types: quotation, purchase order or procurement log
grouping_reasons: one physical space or commission across concept, technical design, specification, purchasing and installation
one property or venue with multiple rooms whose room names and styles are values inside the same project, not separate schemas
one specified item across design tag, supplier quote, purchase order, delivery, installation and warranty evidence
one issue or revision of a drawing/schedule and the transmittal, review, approval or superseded version around it
one handover set whose drawings, schedules, photographs and manuals describe the installed result
one archive packet whose heterogeneous members are grouped by project purpose without copying a property, room or stage fact to sparse members

template.why: The creative schema is a placeholder with no licensed field rows, so this template must recommend no folder dimensions. Interior design nevertheless differs from the creative default by its physical-space lifecycle: a room/property brief is translated into spatial drawings and schedules, then into procurement records and site installation/handover evidence. Space, room, style, material, property and stage remain runtime values or observations until R1c adjudicates shared canonical fields; they must not be smuggled into dimension_order. If fields are later adopted, a sensible order is project or commission, property/venue, stage, then room or artifact type, but that is a future proposal, not a legal current path. The user may reverse, flatten or omit any future order.

collides_with.signal: The same render board or completed-room PDF may be a portfolio case study rather than an active design/procurement record; project issue, schedules, supplier trail or site/handover context distinguishes the active commission.

BIM/CAD files and model exports may sit inside a software repository; repository manifests, source tree and build structure beat room/style vocabulary, while a standalone issued drawing set remains creative.

Site-progress and completed-room images carry capture facts, but EXIF/capture chronology identifies Photos; the interior template requires a design/installation relation and must not infer project or room facts from pixels.

The same specification, drawing, site instruction or handover pack may be part of a construction project; construction/property evidence owns build/contract/site administration, while this template activates on the interior-space design-to-installation brief and its finish/fixture decisions. A room fit-out can be both schemas when both purposes are evidenced.

An improvement cost tracker or invoice can concern the same property; Finance owns household accounting/property administration, while this template requires design/specification/procurement/installation coherence and cannot infer a design project from spend alone.

sensitivity_why: Client addresses, budgets, supplier pricing, access instructions, security-sensitive layouts, unpublished schemes, contractual terms and photographs of occupied homes or workplaces may be sensitive. This posture follows the creative project or property/contract context; no interior-specific handling class or exposure rule is invented.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: Should a future shared canonical key be `property`, `venue`, or a broader `site` for physical-space projects across creative, construction_property, photos and finance? Option A: one shared property/site join (recommended for cross-domain retrieval, with role-bearing validation). Option B: keep the label as group-only and avoid a canonical destination dimension. Option C: split household property from commissioned venue, at the cost of duplicate vocabulary. Until decided, room, address and style remain observations/values and dimension_order stays empty. NEEDS-JOSEPH: Should a completed interior portfolio case study be allowed to also hold the active project, or should the career presentation remain a collision unless source/handover evidence is present?
